newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Kiwi Air deal with BNZ under scrutiny - Wilson.
newsitem.headline: Kiwi Air deal with BNZ under scrutiny - Wilson.

text.p: A police investigation into the collapse of Kiwi International Airlines was focusing on a deal involving the Bank of New Zealand to provide capital for the airline, founder Ewan Wilson told Radio New Zealand on Thursday.
Wilson, speaking from England, said police had spoken to him about three weeks ago regarding the budget trans-Tasman airline's collapse.

"They spoke to me about two issues, both of them to do with the capitalisation of the company, both of them referring back to June of 1995 (when Kiwi Air applied for its international air service licence).
"I think that they're no longer really interested because there was certainly nothing illegal going on."
Wilson said the police had been interested in a "round-robin" deal done between the Bank of New Zealand, an unnamed partnership, and Kiwi International.
The deal had been put together by Kiwi's accountants, Coopers and Lybrand, and the airline's solicitors.
"I am sure they would not have put it together if there was anything illegal about it.

"We certainly didn't think it was illegal and I certainly wouldn't have covered it in such depth in my book (Dogfight: The Inside Story of the Kiwi Airlines Collapse)...if I thought there was anything illegal."
Wilson said police had used a search warrant to seize the original manuscript of the book.
The police investigation had followed inquiries by the Justice Department's commercial affairs division.
Wilson said he was in England holding discussions with aviation contacts. He was due back in New Zealand early Saturday morning.
He said he had cooperated with a Commerce Ministry investigation into the collapse, the results of which are expected later on Thursday. The ministry had not contacted him about its findings.
Police said on Wednesday they were investigating aspects of the airline's liquidation "as a result of documents forwarded to us by another government department". They did not elaborate.
The two-year-old company collapsed in September owing debts of at least NZ$5 million, much of it in pre-paid fares.
Wilson founded Kiwi in 1994 as a trans-Tasman charter airline with Mike Tournier, an air traffic control instructor, American Patrick Pruett, and pilot Mike Park.
Tournier and Park both quit as a directors before the airline collapsed.
